title: Objects, methods and keyword arguments
kicker: Python for SDFs · Read the code

lines.title: Call a function from a library
lines.text: The dot reaches inside the fitz library for its `open` function (the `import fitz` cell already ran). It gives back an object, a Document, that holds the whole PDF.

lines.title: Read an attribute
lines.text: An attribute is a value stored on an object. There are no parentheses: you read it, you don't call it. `page_count` is the number of pages in the document.

lines.title: Pick the first page
lines.text: A Document works like a list of pages, so `[0]` gives you the first one. `page` is another object, a Page.

lines.title: Call a method with an argument
lines.text: A method is a function that belongs to an object, and the parentheses call it. The argument `"words"` asks for a list with one entry per word, including where each word sits on the page.

lines.title: Create an object with a keyword argument
lines.text: `genai.Client(...)` builds a new object that talks to Gemini. `api_key=` is a keyword argument: you name the setting, then give its value. The value comes from another method call, which reads your key from Colab's Secrets.

lines.title: Follow the dots, pass two keyword arguments
lines.text: Read the dots from left to right. The client has a `models` part, and that part has a `generate_content` method. `model=` picks the Gemini model, and `contents=` is what you send it, here the page's text.

lines.title: Read the answer
lines.text: `response` is an object too. Its `text` attribute holds Gemini's reply as a plain string.

predict.question: The sample SDF has 3 pages. What does **line 2** print?

options.feedback: Yes. `page_count` is an attribute that holds how many pages there are. Counts start at 1. It's positions, like `doc[0]`, that start at 0.
That's the position of the last page, because positions start at 0. `page_count` is a count, so it's 3.

options.label: An error, because page_count needs ()
options.feedback: `page_count` is an attribute, not a method, so it takes no parentheses. Writing `doc.page_count()` is what would cause an error.

options.label: The text of all 3 pages
options.feedback: Getting text takes a method call, `get_text()`, on each page. `page_count` holds only a number.

learn.used_later: Project 3 opens SDFs with `fitz.open` and reads `doc.page_count` and `page.get_text("words")`. In Projects 7 and 8, every Gemini call goes through the same `client.models.generate_content(...)` line.
